channel.title: Jiǎoluò Shūwū · 角落書屋
channel.description: A reading nook for Chinese language and civilisation. Characters, vocabulary, grammar, history, philosophy, and the world they shaped.

item.title: 古琴 · the scholar's zither
item.description: The seven-string zither Confucius played throughout his life, and the origin of 知音, the word for a person who truly understands you.

item.title: 生旦净末丑 · Role Types in Peking Opera
item.description: The five 行当 of Peking Opera: sheng, dan, jing, mo, and chou, each a lifelong specialization in voice, movement, and makeup.

item.title: 诗经 · Book of Songs
item.description: The 305 poems of China's oldest anthology (c. 1046-600 BCE), which Confucius said no educated person could afford to ignore.

item.title: 书法风格 · The Five Scripts of Chinese Calligraphy
item.description: The five scripts of Chinese calligraphy, 篆隶楷行草, run from Zhou bronze inscriptions to Tang wild cursive; choosing a script is choosing a register.

item.title: 宋词 · Song Dynasty Lyric
item.description: Song lyrics (词 cí) fit fixed tune patterns called 词牌; Li Qingzhao, Su Shi, and Xin Qiji are the form's three masters.

item.title: 道 · way, path
item.description: The character that opens the Dàodéjīng and names Daoism: way, path, principle, and the measure word for rivers and light.

item.title: 和 · harmony, and, with; peace
item.description: 禾 (grain) beside 口 (mouth): 和 is both Mandarin's everyday "and" and the Confucian ideal of harmony without uniformity.

item.title: 快 · fast, happy
item.description: 快 joins 忄 (heart) to 夬 (a decisive cut): speed and joy are the same image, a heart running without drag.

item.title: 人 · person, humanity
item.description: Two strokes, barely changed since the oracle bones, write 人 rén; add 二 and you get 仁, Confucian benevolence.

item.title: 为 · to do; to act; for; because of
item.description: In oracle bone script 为 is a hand leading an elephant, and it sits at the center of Daoist 无为 non-action.

item.title: 玉 · jade, precious
item.description: Three jade discs on a cord, one dot away from 王 (wáng, king): the stone Confucius said was virtue made visible.

item.title: 了 · the perfective particle
item.description: Post-verb 了 marks a completed action; sentence-final 了 announces a new situation, and the two can stack in one sentence.

item.title: 量词 · measure words
item.description: 个, 只, 条, 本, 张: the classifier taxonomy and the logic behind it.

item.title: 乃 · classical connective: then, thereupon, thus; to be; only then
item.description: Classical 乃 marks a consequence as earned, where modern 就 stays neutral; as emphatic copula it gives 失败乃成功之母 its weight.

item.title: 之 · classical genitive, nominalizer, and pronoun
item.description: 之 zhī did the work of 'of', 'him/her/it', and 'the one who' in classical Chinese; it survives in 之间, 之后, and 总之.

item.title: 者 · classical nominalizer "the one who; that which"
item.description: 者 zhě turns any verb into "the one who": 学者 scholar, 读者 reader, 作者 author, unchanged since the Analects.

item.title: 科举 · The Imperial Examination System
item.description: The exam that selected China's officials for 1,300 years, from the Sui in 605 CE to abolition in 1905.

item.title: 清朝 · The Qing Dynasty
item.description: Invited through Shanhai Pass in 1644, the Manchus ruled China for 268 years, until the 1911 revolution ended imperial rule.

item.title: 宋朝 · The Song Dynasty
item.description: Economic revolution, printing, compass: the dynasty modernity missed.

item.title: 战国时期 · Warring States Period
item.description: Seven states fought from 475 to 221 BCE, and that same fragmentation produced Confucianism, Daoism, Legalism, and Mohism.

item.title: 儒家 · Confucianism
item.description: The school of the ru: ritual, hierarchy, and moral cultivation as state religion.

item.title: 祖先崇拜 · Ancestor Veneration
item.description: Shang oracle bones record divinations to royal ancestors; 祖先崇拜, the ritual care of the dead, continues today in tablets, offerings, and Qingming graves.

item.title: 轮回 · samsara; the cycle of rebirth
item.description: 轮回 renders Sanskrit saṃsāra as 'wheel' plus 'return': the karmic cycle carrying beings through six realms until liberation.

item.title: 缘分 · karmic connection
item.description: Buddhist karmic fate: 500 years of cultivation to share a boat with a stranger, a thousand to share a pillow.

item.title: 禅 · meditation; Chan; to abdicate
item.description: One altar character, two civilizations: read shàn it yields thrones and sacrifices to earth; read chán it transliterates Sanskrit dhyāna and founds Zen.

item.title: 星 · star; celestial body; spark
item.description: Born of the sun radical and a sprout, 星 names the stars, the planets, the week, movie fame, and the spark that starts prairie fires.

item.title: 电脑与网络 · Computers & the Internet
item.description: The computer is an electric brain, downloading is "carrying down," and the number 666 is a compliment.

item.title: 度量衡 · Weights & Measures
item.description: Fruit is priced by the half-kilo 斤, distance walks in 里, and an idiom about six of one and half a dozen still counts in base sixteen.

item.title: 看病 · Seeing a Doctor
item.description: Getting sick in Chinese starts with a queue number, runs on the verb "look," and ends with the eternal prescription: drink more hot water.

item.title: 生意 · Doing Business
item.description: Business in Chinese is literally "the meaning of life," merchants are named after a fallen dynasty, and the deal closes at the dinner table.
